done_when: Windows CI runs only tests marked as platform-sensitive (installers, git hooks, shell quoting, paths, line endings, command stand-ins) on every pull request beside Linux; Linux still runs the whole suite; a test fails when a test in those areas lacks the mark; and a measured Windows run on the branch uses at most 2 times Linux's total runner minutes and at most 2 times Linux's longest group

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The guard searches test bodies only for `branches`, so actual hook tests can remain unmarked without failing it. For example, `tests/test_setup.py:100` defines unmarked `test_28_sync`; lines 169–184 execute commit/push hooks, verify argument forwarding, and verify that a refusing hook blocks the commit. Neither its filename nor function name matches `areas`, and its body contains none of the `branches` patterns. Consequently, Windows now deselects this hook coverage while the new guard passes. Extend detection to cover these hook operations and mark the omitted test.
findings.title: Gate: test_2_platform_sensitive_tests_are_marked

why: Windows CI takes about 6 times Linux (313 against 53 runner minutes, longest group 31.8 against 12.3 minutes) because it runs the whole suite, and it runs only nightly, so Windows bugs show up the next day
